summary: My Utmost for His Highest is a daily Christian devotional compiled from the preaching of Oswald Chambers (1874-1917) to students and soldiers. The note traces its publication history, from a self-published Oxford edition around 1927 to a first American edition by Dodd, Mead, & Co. in 1935 and later revisions. It also notes the title's origin in one of Chambers's sermons and the book's wide influence, including on Cal Thomas and President George W. Bush.
one_line: A daily devotional compiled from Oswald Chambers's Christian preaching, published from 1927 and widely regarded as one of the most popular religious books.
key_facts: My Utmost for His Highest is a daily devotional by Oswald Chambers (1874 - 1917).
The devotional compiles Christian preaching Oswald Chambers gave to students and soldiers.
Chambers' widow self-published the book with Alden in Oxford circa 1927, according to McFarland, "Abandoned to God", 1993, p. 278.
The book was first published in America by Dodd, Mead, & Co., in 1935.
The copyright was renewed in 1963 by the Oswald Chambers Publications Association, Ltd.
The "Updated Edition in Today's Language", edited by James Reimann, has appeared in a variety of formats since 1992.
The updated edition relies on the New King James Version of the Bible.
The book has become a series of Christian devotional journals, calendars, and children's books.
The title is taken from one of Chambers's sermons, where he says "Shut out every consideration and keep yourself before God for this one thing only - My Utmost for His Highest".
The book is considered to be one of the most popular religious books ever written.
The book has inspired several people, including author Cal Thomas and President George W. Bush.
